Select sets the fields to retrieve. Appends fields to SELECT (See example in Model).

The resulting row (the result of `RETURNING`) is used as a source for the `Scan` method, having the DBModel as argument.
Updates uses the same logic of Create (thus the default value handling is the same).
The `RETURNING` clause is handled in the same manner of Create.
The reason is that igor generates queries in the form `SELECT table.field1, table.filed2 FROM table [WHERE] RETURNING table.field1, table.filed2`.
`Scan` handle every type. You can scan query results in:
- a comma separated list of values (because `Scan` is a variadic arguments function) `.Scan(&firstInteger, &firstString, &secondInteger, &floatDestination)`
- `DBModel`: that's the model you want to fill
- `key interface{}` that's the primary key value, that __must__ be of the same type of the `DBModel` primary key.

Protocol Buffers are a language-neutral, platform-neutral extensible mechanism for serializing structured data. Compared to JSON, Protobuf files are smaller and faster to read/write because the data is stored in an efficient binary format.

PufferDB uses a ConcurrentHashMap to manage a thread-safe in-memory cache for fast read and write operations.

By using babashka/ffi to interface with SQLite's C API directly with FFI we bypass the need for: sqlite-jdbc, hikariCP and next.jdbc. This massively reduces the amount of code that needs to be maintained (and a much smaller jar), allows us to use Clojure to interface with SQLite directly. It also makes it easier to add SQLite specific features. In my case I was looking to cache prepared statement for each connection (which is not possible with HikariCP) but can lead to considerable performance gains on complex queries.

Encoding is done with fast-edn as text and then converted into bytes. From my testing this was faster than both deed and nippy despite being a text format. Being a text format it is stable and can be swapped out for faster EDN text serialises without breaking changes. Of course, this also means only EDN data is support and not arbitrary Java classes.
SQLite supports Application-Defined SQL Functions. This lets you extend SQL with clojure defined functions. sqlite4clj streamlines these for interactive use at the repl.
Because SQLite supports Indexes On Expressions and Partial Indexes we can easily index on any arbitrary encoded EDN data.
A partial index is an index over a subset of the rows of a table. This leads to smaller and faster indexes (see Existence Based Processing) when only a subset of the rows have a value you care about.
The bundled library is extracted to a unique temporary file under `java.io.tmpdir` and deleted after it loads.
The library is loaded once and retained across namespace reloads. Set `sqlite4clj.native-lib` before first loading sqlite4clj; changing it requires a JVM restart.

Simkl uses explicit user/media-event checks, persisted activity cursors and baseline/delta observations, with durable watched writes confirmed by provider readback. Unsafe baseline observations stay available to explicit full-sync previews without filling Sync Attention; unsafe new deltas remain visible for review. Eligible concurrent writes share batches of up to 100 with a quota reserve; uncertain outcomes stay held without automatic resend. Ratings that could create watched/list state, unresolved anime/special identity, list-destructive unwatches, paid rewatches and automatic absence reconciliation remain blocked. Plekt retains its full local history independently of provider limits.

Bulk manual watched actions gather Simkl writes into chunks of up to 100, independently of LAN concurrency, and queued captured intents gather up to 100 per run with individual watch-row outcomes. Single watches remain immediate. Batch preflights respect the known quota reserve; failed or invalid preflights save a hold until quota reset, surviving restarts. Four requests apply per chunk; unrelated sequential watches can form separate chunks. Manual full sync requires a one-hour item preview with deselection, fresh-state rechecks and a verified backup. First-run selected history imports start on Continue without a separate preview approval, retaining the backup and freshness guards. Selected imports propagate to their listed media-server destinations; dates already on a destination are preserved. Simkl selected sends show request estimates and retain the quota reserve. Sends audited as missing from Simkl's current progress remain held for review and skipped by later previews. Incremental checks read a separate ratings delta only when rating activity changes, so rating-only edits and explicit clears are captured. After first-run imports finish, the add-only initial outward pass exposes per-destination progress and remaining or held items above Sync / Idle.
